title: Implement OpenAI Realtime gpt-realtime-2 cloud-native S2S provider
description:
Implement OpenAI Realtime gpt-realtime-2 as a SIBLING native-S2S provider, parallel to Gemini Live. Per user's goal correction: gpt-realtime-2 is a native speech-to-speech model (audio in -> audio out) and is NOT a stage in the speech2graph/notes composed pipeline. It is an alternative to Gemini Live, not a stage of the STT->LLM->TTS path.

Scope:
- New module src-tauri/src/openai_realtime/ mirroring gemini/mod.rs shape (WebSocket session, session resumption, reconnect with backoff, error classification, usage tracking).
- Settings enum entry under RealtimeAgent (sibling to GeminiLive), so the UI can route to it without touching ASR/LLM provider enums.
- Tauri commands: start_openai_realtime / stop_openai_realtime, parallel to start_gemini / stop_gemini.
- Frontend event subscription for the new provider events.
- Tests at the same level as gemini::tests.

References:
- docs/adr/0002-openai-realtime-provider.md
- docs/adr/0003-speech-to-speech-agent-provider-matrix.md
- src-tauri/src/gemini/mod.rs (~90KB; pattern to follow)
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-realtime-2

Out of scope: composed-pipeline orchestration (separate issue eee3 — different architectural path), barge-in semantics across providers (separate issue 7fcc), eager turn detection (separate issue 82b3).

title: Add TtsProvider trait + Deepgram Aura streaming TTS
description:
ADR-0003 names TTS as a first-class provider category for the speech-to-speech personality — Deepgram Aura, Kokoro, Piper, Coqui — but no implementation exists. TTS is the missing leg of the local/hybrid S2S pipeline (STT -> vLLM -> TTS).

Scope:
- New module src-tauri/src/tts/ with a TtsProvider trait. Stream-shaped (chunked PCM audio with playback timing, support cancellation/barge-in).
- First implementation: DeepgramAura over WebSocket, parallel to existing asr/deepgram.rs.
- Settings enum entry TtsProvider with variants None / DeepgramAura / Local* (stubbed).
- Wire provider into the S2S turn orchestrator (separate issue) once that lands.
- Tauri commands: test_tts_connection_cmd, list_tts_voices_cmd.
- Frontend types + credentials allowlist sync.

References:
- docs/adr/0003-speech-to-speech-agent-provider-matrix.md (provider matrix)
- src-tauri/src/asr/deepgram.rs (54KB; shape to mirror)
- https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/tts-websocket

Out of scope: Kokoro/Piper/Coqui local TTS engines (separate issues), barge-in semantics (separate issue).

title: Local/hybrid S2S pipeline: STT -> vLLM -> TTS turn orchestrator
description:
Composed-pipeline speech-to-speech orchestrator: STT -> LLM (OpenRouter or local vLLM) -> TTS (Deepgram Aura or local). This is the LOCAL/HYBRID composed pipeline only — NOT a wrapper around Gemini Live or gpt-realtime-2.

Goal alignment: this orchestrator drives the optional 'voice2voice agent that works in parallel to the initial speech2graph pipeline'. The initial pipeline (STT -> graph/notes + chatbot replies) already runs from the same STT source; this orchestrator adds the option of speaking-aloud agent replies.

Scope:
- New module src-tauri/src/s2s_local/ (or rename to src-tauri/src/voice_agent/) with a TurnState struct: source id, provider ids, sample rate, start timestamp, cancellation token, bounded audio + token buffers.
- Turn protocol: turn_start, audio append, turn_end, cancel. (barge_in is a separate issue.)
- Wires existing ASR finals -> existing OpenAI-compatible LLM (OpenRouter or local vLLM via HTTP) -> new TtsProvider -> audio playback.
- Latency milestone events: turn start, first STT partial, STT final, LLM request start, first LLM token, first TTS audio, final TTS audio, cancel ack.
- Frontend: surface latency milestones beside existing pipeline-latency status.
- Tauri commands: start_voice_agent, stop_voice_agent.

Hard dependencies: TtsProvider trait + at least one TTS impl (3132); audio playback subsystem (8d75); OpenRouter wired (c847) so the agent has a real LLM.

Out of scope: Gemini Live (already shipped), gpt-realtime-2 (separate issue 396f) — those are native-S2S models and bypass this orchestrator entirely.

References:
- docs/adr/0003 turn protocol section
- ../HF/streaming-speech-to-speech (HF reference impl; do not port wholesale)

queue_lane_2026_06_25.cutline: P1 once core transcript/projection and playback prerequisites are green
queue_lane_2026_06_25.summary: Owns the composed STT -> LLM -> TTS voice-agent path. It remains separate from native S2S providers and depends on local/cloud STT readiness, playback resampling, and local/cloud TTS availability.

title: Local TTS providers: Kokoro, Piper, Coqui
description:
Once TtsProvider trait lands, add local TTS engines for fully local S2S pipeline. Each is a separate impl behind a cargo feature flag (tts-kokoro, tts-piper, tts-coqui).

Scope (per provider):
- ONNX or other binding crate selection.
- Voice model bundling / download script update (scripts/download-models.ps1).
- Streaming chunk emission compatible with TtsProvider trait.

Out of scope: TtsProvider trait itself (separate issue).

title: Deepgram Flux EagerEndOfTurn support with TurnResumed rollback
description:
ADR-0003 'Deepgram + local turn strategy' notes EagerEndOfTurn can shave latency by starting LLM/TTS work before the high-confidence EndOfTurn, with TurnResumed as the rollback signal.

Scope:
- Wire Flux events through to S2S turn orchestrator.
- On EagerEndOfTurn: start LLM/TTS speculatively; capture cancel token.
- On TurnResumed: cancel speculative LLM/TTS work, wait for next final/eager event.
- UI surfaces eager-turn count + false-start (TurnResumed) count so users can tune.
- Telemetry: emit per-turn 'speculative cancelled' events for latency dashboards.

Hard dependency: S2S turn orchestrator must exist first.

title: Barge-in / interruption support across S2S providers
description:
ADR-0003 wave 5 — interruption semantics for Gemini Live, OpenAI Realtime, and the local pipeline.

Scope:
- Cancel current LLM/TTS output when a new turn starts.
- Stop UI playback immediately.
- Emit cancel-acknowledgement event before allowing the next turn.
- Immediate-retry guards so user can't double-trigger.
- Per-provider implementation: each S2S provider needs its own cancel path.

Hard dependency: at least the turn protocol from the local S2S epic.

title: Document GraphDelta dual-emission contract or unify to single channel
description:
Project-mapping audit found backend emits both full graph-update snapshots (~10s throttle) AND incremental graph-delta events (per-extraction). UI may be optimized for deltas; dual-emission could cause reconciliation bugs.

Scope:
- Decide: keep both (with explicit contract) or consolidate to delta-only with on-demand snapshot.
- If keeping both: write src-tauri/src/events.rs doc-comment specifying the ordering invariant (e.g. 'a snapshot supersedes any deltas with timestamp <= snapshot.timestamp').
- Frontend: verify the React graph store applies them in the right order; add a vitest if not covered.

Found during Wave 1 mapping; surfaced as an architectural risk, not a confirmed bug.
closeReason: Documented the graph-update/graph-delta ordering contract in Rust and TS: deltas are incremental best-effort updates between authoritative snapshots, and snapshots supersede prior deltas. Added store regression coverage that snapshots replace canonical graph state after earlier deltas. Verified typecheck, Biome, focused store tests, and cargo check.

triage_2026_08_14.agent_brief:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Reconcile AudioGraph onto the newest stable rsac release while preserving immutable, cross-platform dependency resolution.

**Current behavior:**
The main branch pins official rsac v0.4.1 even though v0.4.4 is the newest stable release as of 2026-08-14. Verified v0.4.4 integration commits exist in repository history, but the main branch does not contain them. Older duplicate tracking describes sibling checkouts or tagged SHAs without owning the complete Cargo, lockfile, CI, release-attestation, documentation, and platform-evidence contract.

**Desired behavior:**
At integration time, resolve the newest stable official rsac release, pin its full immutable commit in every target-specific Cargo dependency, commit the resulting application lockfile, and make locked Cargo resolution the only build and release authority. Never float a branch or mutable tag. A newer stable release discovered before integration supersedes v0.4.4 only after compatibility and platform gates pass.

**Key interfaces:**
- Target-specific rsac dependency declarations — all desktop targets must resolve the same immutable release commit with only approved features.
- Application dependency lock — must capture the exact Git source and remain authoritative in local, CI, and release builds.
- CI and release attestation — must derive version and revision from locked Cargo metadata instead of independent SHA inputs.
- Capture capability contract — must preserve consent, timestamp, drop, format-change, and platform behavior required by AudioGraph.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The official releases page is checked at integration time and the newest stable rsac release is selected.
- [ ] Linux, Windows, and macOS dependencies pin the same full immutable commit and the committed lockfile resolves it under --locked.
- [ ] Existing verified v0.4.4 integration work is semantically reused where applicable rather than reimplemented blindly.
- [ ] Locked metadata, compile, focused capture tests, format, and strict Clippy pass locally where supported.
- [ ] Windows and macOS CI/capture evidence is recorded, along with Linux evidence.
- [ ] Release dry-run attestation reports exactly the Cargo-resolved rsac version and revision.
- [ ] No mobile, private macOS SPI, compose, or unrelated rsac feature is enabled accidentally.

**Out of scope:**
- Floating on rsac main, a mutable tag, or an unpinned sibling checkout.
- Automatically accepting future rsac releases without compatibility and platform verification.
- Changing AudioGraph's capture product behavior beyond compatibility work required by the selected stable release.

title: Move set_var(GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS) out of Vertex AI hot path
description:
Test suite auditor flagged src-tauri/src/gemini/mod.rs:762 — production code calls 'set_var(GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, ...)' inside the VertexAI auth path. This mutates process-global env without restoring; any test that exercises Vertex auth leaks the value.

Scope:
- Replace with per-request credential file path passed via Vertex SDK config object, not env var.
- Or, if the Google auth library only reads the env var, isolate the mutation behind a Mutex + restore-on-drop guard.

Severity: medium — currently no test hits this path, but it's a latent landmine.
closeReason: Replaced the Vertex AI explicit service-account path flow in gemini::open_ws with gcp_auth::CustomServiceAccount::from_file, then token() directly, so GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is no longer mutated in the Gemini hot path. The default/no-path flow still uses gcp_auth::provider() for ADC/gcloud behavior. Verified rg shows no GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS mutation remains in gemini, cargo fmt, focused Gemini test, cargo check --lib, cargo check --lib --features diarization-clustering, and git diff --check with only pre-existing CRLF warnings.

title: Wire OpenRouter as the default cloud LLM for the primary pipeline
description:
Goal-aligned: OpenRouter is the chosen cloud LLM for the speech2graph/notes pipeline (STT -> T2T -> TTS).

OpenRouter is OpenAI-compatible HTTP, so the existing 'Api' LLM provider variant should serve it with base URL pointed at openrouter.ai/api/v1. But credentials/test-connection wiring needs an OpenRouter-specific path.

Scope:
- New OpenRouter provider variant (or first-class config preset for the existing Api variant) so the UI surfaces 'OpenRouter' separately from generic 'OpenAI-compatible'.
- Credentials: api key with allowlist update in src/types/index.ts and src-tauri/src/credentials/mod.rs.
- test_openrouter_connection_cmd Tauri command, parallel to test_deepgram_connection.
- Settings UI: model picker that calls OpenRouter's /models endpoint to populate.
- Frontend: route the chatbot/agent's LLM calls through OpenRouter when configured.
- Ensure HTTP referrer/X-Title headers per OpenRouter docs (they're free + provide attribution).

Acceptance: a fresh install can pick OpenRouter, paste an API key, choose a model, and have the chatbot reply through it. Same pattern as Deepgram setup today.

title: Audio playback for TTS responses (Windows + Linux)
description:
Goal-aligned: chatbot replies must be played aloud as TTS audio. Today there is no audio output path; only audio capture via rsac.

Scope:
- Choose a cross-platform audio output crate (cpal, rodio, kira). cpal is most likely the right call given rsac probably already pulls it.
- Backend: receive PCM chunks from the TtsProvider stream and feed them to an output stream.
- Frontend: optional waveform/level meter; subscribe to playback events for UI affordances (mute, pause).
- Cancellation: a new turn / barge-in must stop playback within ~50ms.
- Format negotiation: TtsProvider yields PCM at a stated sample rate; resampler if device doesn't support it natively.
- Tauri commands: start_playback / stop_playback / set_output_device.

Hard dependency: TtsProvider trait (audio-graph-3132).

Linux + Windows are the priority targets per goal; macOS deferred.

title: Connect chatbot replies to TTS playback (the speak-aloud loop)
description:
Goal-aligned: when the chatbot/agent generates a reply via OpenRouter, route the streaming text to the TtsProvider, which plays via the new playback subsystem. This closes the STT->T2T->TTS loop.

Scope:
- Subscribe to LLM token deltas (already emitted as part of chat).
- Aggressive token-to-TTS flushing as ADR-0003 'turn protocol' specifies.
- Settings flag: enable speak-aloud per session.
- UI affordance: a speaker icon next to chatbot replies; click to replay.
- Cancellation propagation: user canceling a chatbot reply also cancels TTS.

Hard dependencies: TtsProvider (3132), audio playback (new), OpenRouter wiring (new).

title: Moonshine streaming STT provider (local)
description:
Goal-aligned: a low-latency local streaming STT option for the primary pipeline, alongside existing Whisper/Sherpa.

Scope:
- Pick a Rust binding or run via ONNX Runtime (moonshine-onnx publishes weights).
- Hook into existing Asr provider trait (whichever it is — see src-tauri/src/asr/).
- Streaming partial+final transcript emission with normalized turn lifecycle events (per ADR-0003 turn-detection contract).
- Behind cargo feature flag asr-moonshine so it doesn't bloat the default build.
- Voice activity / endpointing strategy: documented in the ADR for the local pipeline (audio-graph-eee3).

Out of scope: training, fine-tuning. Just inference.

References:
- https://github.com/usefulsensors/moonshine
- /mnt/e/CS/HF/streaming-speech-to-speech for streaming patterns

title: Document local LLM topology: vLLM external server with CUDA graphs
description:

The user's note: '8B or less model locally with vllm and cuda graphs and our s2s pipeline'. vLLM speaks the OpenAI-compatible API, so AudioGraph's existing 'Api' LLM provider variant works — but the configuration story (CUDA graphs flags, recommended models, base URL) needs documentation so contributors can run a local pipeline reproducibly.

title: Windows cargo test fails: rustc-link-arg-tests= without [[test]] target
description:
Wave 1 commit 7fd608f changed build.rs from rustc-link-arg= to rustc-link-arg-tests= to scope the test manifest embedding to test binaries only.

But the audio-graph crate has no [[test]] target in Cargo.toml — its tests live inline in #[cfg(test)] mod blocks within the [lib]. Cargo rejects rustc-link-arg-tests= in this case with:

  invalid instruction `cargo::rustc-link-arg-tests` from build script of `audio-graph v0.1.0`
  The package audio-graph v0.1.0 does not have a test target.

Failure: Windows job in run 26130224852.

Fix options:
  1. Revert build.rs to unscoped rustc-link-arg= (loses defense-in-depth but works).
  2. Add an explicit [[test]] target in Cargo.toml so -tests= is valid.
  3. Use a different gate.

Recommend (1) with a guard: if the env var is set AND we're building a non-test target, panic at build time so we fail loudly rather than embedding the manifest into a production exe.

References:
- src-tauri/build.rs (the offending println line)
- Cargo book: build script outputs

title: Aura: session-layer barge-in suppression of in-flight AudioChunk frames
description:
Reviewer A1+A2 (2026-05-20) flagged HIGH: clear_drops_in_flight_audio_frames test asserts only that the Cleared ack arrives, NOT that audio frames received between the client-side Clear send and the Cleared ack are suppressed. The barge-in contract is currently placed entirely on the consumer with no enforcing mechanism in the session layer.

Fix: AuraSession's session task should set an Arc<AtomicBool> clearing flag when SessionCmd::Clear is dispatched, clear it when Cleared is received. AudioChunk events emitted while the flag is set should be suppressed (or tagged with a cancelled: bool field). The test should then assert trailing_audio_count == 0.

Why P1: this is a Wave-B blocker. The audio playback subsystem will produce audible 'tail' artifacts on barge-in if the session layer doesn't suppress trailing frames.

References: docs/reviews/audio-graph-wave-a-review.md (or commit message of the next review-summary commit), src-tauri/src/tts/deepgram_aura.rs around line 1154-1160.

title: Aura: run session task on caller's runtime in tests for tokio::time::pause()
description:
Reviewer A1+A2 (2026-05-20) flagged MEDIUM: keepalive_sent_after_idle_timeout test waits ~12s wall-clock because the session task spawns its own new_multi_thread runtime that tokio::time::pause() can't drive. Inflates cargo test --lib tts wall-clock by ~12s every CI run.

Fix: factor a #[cfg(test)] AuraSession::start_with_url_on_current_runtime constructor that uses tokio::spawn (caller's runtime) rather than a dedicated runtime. Then tokio::time::pause() and tokio::time::advance() drive the test instantly.

References: src-tauri/src/tts/deepgram_aura.rs:1163-1226 (test) + spawn_session.

title: Aura: flush_seq has tearing race across rapid concurrent flushes
description:
Reviewer A1+A2 (2026-05-20) flagged LOW: flush() increments flush_seq atomically before sending SessionCmd::Flush. Session task reads flush_seq.load(SeqCst) when server sends Flushed. If caller calls flush() twice before the first Flushed ack arrives, both acks report the same sequence value (post-second-increment).

Fix: send the seq value INSIDE the enum variant — SessionCmd::Flush(u64) — and use the dispatch-time snapshot on the ack side, rather than re-reading the shared atomic.

Currently harmless (no consumer depends on the sequence number) but worth fixing before any does. References: src-tauri/src/tts/deepgram_aura.rs:264 + 722-724.
closeReason: Fixed Aura flush ack tearing by carrying dispatch-time sequence in SessionCmd::Flush, queueing pending flush sequences in the session loop, and adding focused non-socket regressions.

title: Streaming chat for LocalLlama, MistralRs, AwsBedrock providers
description:
Plan A3 (streaming chat) was scoped on its retry to ONLY the Api + OpenRouter providers. The LocalLlama (engine.rs), MistralRs (mistralrs_engine.rs), and AwsBedrock providers still use blocking chat.

Scope:
- LocalLlama: use llama.cpp's existing token-callback API to emit deltas through the executor's event_tx.
- MistralRs: use its existing streaming token API.
- AwsBedrock: use Bedrock ConverseStream API. Different SSE shape than OpenAI; needs an adapter.

Each provider can be a separate PR. Until done, the speak-aloud loop (audio-graph-92c7) only works with cloud LLMs (Api / OpenRouter) — local LLM users will see blocking-then-batch TTS instead of streaming TTS.

References: docs/adr/0006-streaming-chat-and-native-s2s-separation.md, docs/research/chat-tts-integration-map.md, plan A3.

title: Streaming chat: propagate finish_reason from provider through TokenDelta::Done
description:
Reviewer A3 (2026-05-20) flagged HIGH: commands.rs:1229 hardcodes finish_reason: 'stop' in chat-token-done payload. The actual provider finish_reason ('stop' / 'length' / 'content_filter') lives in the last TokenDelta::Delta but is never threaded into Done.

Why P1: Wave C's speak-aloud loop will incorrectly treat a 'length' (truncated reply) as a successful stop. The frontend type ChatTokenDoneEvent already advertises these values.

Fix: thread the last-seen non-null finish_reason from the Delta stream into TokenDelta::Done. Either add finish_reason: Option<String> to the Done variant or capture it in a local during run_sse_stream and pass it on the Done emission.

References: src-tauri/src/llm/streaming.rs run_sse_stream around line 317; src-tauri/src/commands.rs:1229; src-tauri/src/llm/streaming.rs:55-57 (Done variant declaration); src/types/index.ts:870 (ChatTokenDoneEvent.finish_reason field comment).

title: SSE parser: cap SseDecoder.buf to prevent unbounded growth on malicious streams
description:
Reviewer A3 (2026-05-20) flagged LOW: SseDecoder.buf is a Vec<u8> with no size cap. A malicious or broken upstream that never emits \n\n will grow the buffer indefinitely, exhausting memory.

Fix: add a configurable max-frame-size guard (e.g. 1 MB). On overflow, emit SseEvent::Error or similar and discard the buffer.

References: src-tauri/src/llm/sse.rs SseDecoder + feed().
closeReason: Implemented bounded SseDecoder frame cap with explicit overflow error event, streaming consumer handling, and focused llm::sse tests.

title: StreamRegistry::cancel: document TOCTOU window in return-value semantics
description:
Reviewer A3 (2026-05-20) flagged MEDIUM: StreamRegistry removes the cancel token under the lock then calls .cancel() outside the lock. If the stream task's terminal arm calls registry.finish() between the remove and the external cancel, the boolean cancel() returns true even though Done already arrived.

Not a data-corruption bug, but the boolean return is unreliable. Fix: doc-comment the return value as 'best-effort' and clarify Cancelled is not guaranteed to be the next terminal frame.

References: src-tauri/src/llm/streaming.rs StreamRegistry::cancel near line 483-497.
closeReason: Clarified CancellationToken drop behavior in the blocking chat shim and documented StreamRegistry::cancel as a best-effort return value.

title: send_chat_message shim: clarify cancel token drop semantics
description:
Reviewer A3 (2026-05-20) flagged LOW: commands.rs:1382 binds cancel token as _cancel which is dropped at scope end. Dropping a tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken does NOT fire it — but a future reader may misread this as cancellation-on-drop.

Fix: rename to _no_cancel or add a comment: '// CancellationToken does not fire on drop; this binding silences unused-result warnings while keeping the cancel infrastructure intact.'

References: src-tauri/src/commands.rs:1382.
closeReason: Clarified CancellationToken drop behavior in the blocking chat shim and documented StreamRegistry::cancel as a best-effort return value.

title: Gate local ML (whisper-rs, llama-cpp-2, mistralrs) behind cargo feature flags
description:
Per ADR-0007. Original problem: the three native ML crates were non-optional, so every build compiled whisper.cpp + llama.cpp + mistral.rs and required the local native ML toolchain even for cloud-only users. Step 1 scope: make deps optional, add asr-whisper/llm-llama/llm-mistralrs plus local-ml umbrella default, cfg-gate call sites with graceful provider-unavailable errors, and add a cloud-only CI job. Step 2 follow-up: flip default to cloud-only.

Audit 2026-06-24: code side is implemented. src-tauri/Cargo.toml has default = local-ml, cloud marker, optional whisper-rs/llama-cpp-2/mistralrs deps, and weak cuda/vulkan feature refs. cargo tree --no-default-features --features cloud -i whisper-rs / llama-cpp-2 / mistralrs returns package-not-found for all three, confirming the cloud feature graph excludes the heavy local engines. Existing cfg stubs return clear provider-unavailable behavior for local Whisper/llama/mistral builds.

Remaining acceptance: a dedicated cloud-only Rust CI job is not present in .github/workflows/ci.yml as inspected on 2026-06-24. CI edits are approval-gated for this session, so this issue now depends on audio-graph-150f / the Blacksmith CI matrix work. Also still needs a full cloud-only test run in CI or an equivalent documented local run before closure. Acceptance: cargo build/check/test --no-default-features --features cloud passes in the CI matrix without linking whisper-rs, llama-cpp-2, or mistralrs, and the workflow exposes that gate clearly.

title: Debug build trips _CrtIsValidHeapPointer assertion on Windows (mixed CRT)
description: A --debug Tauri build (debug CRT /MDd) crashes at runtime with a 'Debug Assertion Failed! _CrtIsValidHeapPointer(block)' dialog (debug_heap.cpp:904). Root cause: bundled native ML libs (whisper.cpp/llama.cpp/mistral.rs) are compiled by cc/CMake against the release CRT (/MD), so a buffer allocated in one CRT is freed by the other; the debug CRT validates this and aborts. Release builds share one CRT and run fine. Workaround documented in docs/WINDOWS_QUICKSTART.md (use release). Proper fixes to evaluate: force the C++ deps to build with the matching CRT in debug (CFLAGS /MDd via cc/cmake), or set crt-static consistently, or feature-gate local ML out of debug runs (see ADR-0007 / issue 5fe7). Lower priority than 5fe7 since release works.

queue_reorg_2026_06_25.summary: Lowered from P2 to P3 because the Seed itself records release builds work and the failure is limited to debug CRT/local-ML skew; keep tracked but outside the immediate cross-platform release cutline.

closeReason: FIXED + PROVEN on Windows. CI job rust-windows-debug-crt-smoke (ci.yml run 28360916441, commit c22d564) is GREEN: built the --debug local-ml Tauri app AND ran the debug whisper lib tests (heap-exercising) on blacksmith-4vcpu-windows-2025 with NO is_block_type_valid abort. Fix = force native ML deps to /MDd: CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY=MultiThreadedDebugDLL + LLAMA_LIB_PROFILE=Debug (llama) + per-config CMAKE_{C,CXX}_FLAGS_{RELEASE,RELWITHDEBINFO}=/MDd + base CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS=/MDd (whisper hardcodes RelWithDebInfo). Scoped to Windows+debug only via the CI job + scripts/run-windows-debug.ps1 wrapper — config.toml [env] NOT used (can't cfg-scope), so release/Linux/macOS untouched. Two iters: iter-1 LNK2038 (base flags missed per-config injection) -> iter-2 green. docs/ops/windows-debug-crt-fix.md + WINDOWS_QUICKSTART updated; build.rs emits a guard warning. Release builds were always fine (single CRT).

title: cargo test harness binary fails to launch on Windows (STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND)
description: On this Windows machine, the release/debug app binary runs fine but the cargo unit-test harness binary (target/*/deps/audio_graph-*.exe) exits with 0xc0000139 STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND before any test runs, so cargo test --lib cannot execute Rust unit tests. PE import parse of the test exe shows imports: standard system DLLs + MSVCP140/VCRUNTIME140/VCRUNTIME140_1 + VCOMP140.DLL (MSVC OpenMP, pulled by whisper/llama/ggml). System32 copies are current (14.51.36231.0), so not a stale redist; a dependent DLL is missing an expected entrypoint only in the larger test-harness link. Workaround: verify Rust logic via the release app + targeted example/CLI runs; frontend tests (vitest, 148) run fine. Investigate: dumpbin /dependents + /imports on the test exe under a VS dev shell to find the missing symbol; candidate causes: VCOMP140 OpenMP version, or a delay-load. Blocks write tests for every section on the Rust side until resolved.
closeReason: Stale: docs/ops/windows-rust-test-crt-skew.md now marks the native Windows cargo test harness issue SOLVED via AUDIOGRAPH_EMBED_WINDOWS_TEST_MANIFEST=1, and .github/workflows/ci.yml uses that env var in the Blacksmith rust-windows cargo test job.

title: Streaming transcript to notes and temporal-graph diff pipeline
description: Replace append-only transcript-derived notes/graph behavior with an event-sourced diff/retcon pipeline. Transcription remains saved durably, while notes and graph nodes/relationships are generated as versioned patches from transcript windows. A TTFT/backpressure-aware LLM queue batches incoming finalized turns, waits for in-flight synthesis when needed, merges new context, and emits notes/graph diffs with provenance. Acceptance: transcript JSONL is immutable source of truth; notes and graph state are patchable/versioned; frontend can display updates/retcons; evaluation harness measures latency, diff quality, and graph stability on recorded sessions.

dynamic_queue_architecture_reconciliatio.summary: Current code has already implemented the core non-append-only architecture the user envisioned: immutable TranscriptEvent JSONL, revisioned TranscriptLedger basis, TTFT-aware ProjectionScheduler, structured ProjectionPatch generation, validated notes/graph materializers, accepted patch replay, frontend transcript/notes/graph reducers, and projection diagnostics. title: Backend provider capability registry with TS schema generation
description: Introduce a backend-owned provider registry for ASR, LLM, TTS, Gemini/RealtimeAgent, and future providers. Registry entries declare provider id, family/stage, display key, settings variant, implementation status, transport, credential key/auth kind, required feature flags, sample-rate/audio requirements, source policy, streaming support, partial/final/turn semantics, model catalog strategy, health-check command, defaults, and UI schema groups: basic, advanced, health, modelCatalog. title: Saved-credential health checks and model discovery on Settings open
description: When Settings opens, use saved credentials from credentials.yaml through backend-only provider health/model commands; do not pass plaintext secrets back into React for normal health/model discovery. Scope: add backend-owned provider readiness cache, get_provider_readiness command, provider health probes, model/voice/language discovery with TTL/debounce, cancellation/rate limiting, in-flight coalescing, cached failures, and refresh after save/clear. Cache keys must exclude API keys and use provider id plus non-secret config (endpoint/base URL, AWS region/source/profile) plus a credential epoch incremented by save_credential_cmd/delete_credential_cmd. title: Live rsac audio smoke tests on CI-capable runners
description:
Add gated live audio capture smokes using virtual devices where CI runners support them. Scope: Linux PipeWire dummy sink/source, Windows VB-CABLE or loopback fixture, macOS BlackHole/native loopback if available; test system/default/device/process capture enough to catch source-id and format-negotiation regressions. Acceptance: workflow_dispatch and scheduled jobs can run live smokes; normal PRs keep lightweight checks; failures attach source/device enumeration logs.

--- RESEARCH COMPLETE 2026-06-27 (docs/research/ci-virtual-audio-devices-2026-06-27.md) ---
ADOPT (do not build) on all 3 OSes. Baseline: LABSN/sound-ci-helpers (BSD-3, one composite action, all 3 OSes, maintained 2026-06-22).

LINUX: PipeWire null-sink + .monitor capture-back. CRITICAL: snd-aloop/snd-dummy CANNOT load on GitHub-hosted runners (Azure VM kernel has no sound support; GitHub confirmed no plans Feb 2026). Userspace PipeWire is the ONLY hosted path — and it is what rsac actually enumerates (rsac Linux capture = PipeWire, not raw ALSA). CI already installs PipeWire from PPA. Add a .monitor shim since LABSN's Pulse-only Linux path doesn't guarantee capture-back.

MACOS: BlackHole 2ch (brew install blackhole-2ch + sudo killall coreaudiod). User-space CoreAudio AudioServerPlugin (HAL plugin), NOT a kext -> no SIP change, no kext approval, no reboot. GitHub preinstalls it but it flakes ~30% so install explicitly. macOS 14.4+ uses 'killall coreaudiod' not 'kickstart -k'. GPLv3.

WINDOWS: VB-CABLE (cert-pretrust into TrustedPublisher -> silent -i -h install -> net start audiosrv). Silent unattended install proven on stock GH runners (freedv-gui, AlekseyMartynov action). CRITICAL: bare Windows runners have NO audio device + audio service off; WASAPI loopback alone is NOT a substitute (GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender) returns ERROR_NOT_FOUND with no hw) -> a virtual driver is mandatory. LICENSING CAVEAT: VB-Audio expects a paid license for automated/server use -> resolve before relying on it in CI.

Nothing requires self-hosting on hosted runners; Blacksmith's only edge is pre-baking certs/drivers to cut per-job time/flakiness. cpal (our playback dep) does NO real-device CI -> audio-graph would be ahead of upstream; LABSN is the closest community pattern.

IMPL PATH: gate behind a 'live-audio-smoke' Cargo feature + workflow_dispatch/scheduled (mirror the existing optional-feature matrix gating); PRs keep lightweight checks; attach enumeration logs on failure. Follow-up: resolve VB-CABLE licensing for CI use.

title: TTFT-aware LLM synthesis queue for notes and graph diffs
description: Implement a backend ProjectionScheduler that batches transcript deltas into TTFT/backpressure-aware LLM synthesis jobs without overlapping incompatible calls. Strategy: partial ASR updates revise the transcript ledger; stable/final spans enqueue projection work; while an LLM call is in flight, coalesce new spans and repair windows; each response emits structured patch proposals tied to a ProjectionJob basis {span_ids, revision_numbers, transcript_hash}; stale responses are discarded or converted into repair jobs. Scope: provider latency/TTFT metrics, bounded queues, cancellation/retcon, deterministic coalescing tests, and hooks into existing LLM executor without blocking chat. Acceptance: no LLM call is made per partial token; canonical notes/graph update through patches with provenance; queue telemetry shows lag/coalescing/stale-discard counts.

title: Speaker timeline to channel-aware ASR projection

Scope: define when to use provider diarization, local diarization, or hybrid reconciliation; map DiarizationSpan/SpeakerTimeline revisions onto normalized ASR span revisions; evaluate channel-aware providers that can consume separate audio channels; if feasible, build a bounded speaker-channel mux that projects stable local speaker IDs into per-speaker or per-source PCM lanes without breaking timing, overlap handling, backpressure, or provider sample-rate/channel limits. Must support flexible/unknown speaker counts, but cap exported physical/provider channels per provider and preserve overflow/overlap metadata. Acceptance: provider descriptors declare diarization support and channel handling; local diarization can enrich ASR events without re-transcribing; providers with multi-channel support can opt into deterministic channel projection; replay fixtures prove speaker remaps generate revisions/diffs rather than duplicate transcript entries.

title: LocalLlama token-callback streaming and interruptible cancellation
description: Follow-up from audio-graph-e2b6. The current LocalLlama streaming compatibility adapter uses the existing blocking LlmEngine::chat path and emits one honest full-text delta, so cancellation finalizes the wrapper/UI but cannot interrupt llama.cpp inference once decode starts. Scope: expose token callback streaming from the persistent-context actor without moving LlamaContext across threads; emit real TokenDelta pieces; check CancellationToken between generated tokens; release the local engine promptly on cancel; preserve blocking chat behavior and token usage telemetry. The correct callback point is AudioGraph owned: engine.rs already samples one token, converts it with token_to_piece, appends it, and decodes the next token on the existing actor thread. Implement true LocalLlama streaming by adding an EngineReq::StreamChat path and emitting local stream events from that loop while checking cancellation between tokens.

Keep StreamBackendHandles boundary unchanged and keep executor.rs blocking chat on engine.chat.
Do not hold Arc<Mutex<Option<LlmEngine>>> for the whole stream; clone the lightweight engine sender handle under the mutex and drop the guard before waiting.

title: First-class Cerebras OpenAI-compatible LLM provider readiness
description:
Cerebras is not currently a first-class AudioGraph LLM provider. Local code exposes LocalLlama, generic OpenAI-compatible Api, OpenRouter, AwsBedrock, and MistralRs, so users can likely point the generic Api provider at https://api.cerebras.ai/v1, but Settings cannot show Cerebras-specific provider metadata, saved-key health/model discovery, defaults, or recovery guidance.

Scope:
- Add a Cerebras LLM provider descriptor or provider-registry metadata path for the OpenAI-compatible Cerebras endpoint.
- Decide whether this should be a new LlmProvider enum variant or a typed preset over the generic Api provider. Prefer the least invasive path that still enables saved-key readiness/model catalog and clear Settings UX.
- Store any Cerebras key only in credentials.yaml / local credential backend, never config.yaml, logs, screenshots, docs, or Seeds.
- Add backend-owned health/model discovery if Cerebras exposes a safe endpoint; otherwise mark the provider as saved-key present with explicit no-probe/catalog limitations.
- Add Settings tests proving saved credential presence enables model/provider controls without plaintext key readback.

Acceptance:
- Cerebras appears as a clear LLM provider/preset with endpoint/default model metadata.
- Saved credentials are detected and can drive health/model readiness without re-entering the key.
- Generic Api behavior remains available for arbitrary OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- Cross-platform Tauri/Settings tests pass without secret leakage.

References checked 2026-06-25:
- Cerebras OpenAI compatibility docs: https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/resources/openai
- Current code: src-tauri/src/settings/mod.rs LlmProvider and src-tauri/src/provider_registry.rs LLM provider descriptors

title: Competitive product roadmap: overtake Granola and Cluely
description:
Later-roadmap umbrella for making AudioGraph stronger than Granola-style AI notetaking and Cluely-style live assistance after the core cross-platform capture, credentials, transcript, notes, graph, diarization, and provider platform are stable.

Competitive target checked 2026-06-25: Granola emphasizes bot-free computer-audio capture, calendar briefs, searchable memory, sharing, and privacy/security; Cluely emphasizes live real-time answers, meeting notes, modes, transcript/live-insight cards, and desktop/mobile availability.

Goal: define product and architecture work that compounds on AudioGraph's durable transcript/notes/temporal-graph foundation instead of copying competitors superficially. This epic should stay P2/later-roadmap until the P1 usable cross-platform cutline is green.

Acceptance:
- Child Seeds cover pre-meeting, in-meeting, post-meeting, trust/privacy, collaboration, integrations, and benchmark loops.
- Every feature is compatible with local-first/cross-platform architecture and saved credential rules.
- Competitive work is measured by repeatable quality/latency/usability benchmarks, not only UI claims.

title: Competitive benchmark suite for notes, memory, and live assist quality
description:
Create a repeatable evaluation harness that compares AudioGraph against Granola, Cluely, Otter, Fireflies, Fathom, and platform-native meeting assistants.

Scope:
- Define transcript accuracy, speaker attribution, note usefulness, action-item precision/recall, decision capture, hallucination rate, live-assist latency, time-to-first-note, and sharing/privacy criteria.
- Use fixture meetings across sales, product research, engineering standup, recruiting, support, and in-person conversations.
- Score AudioGraph generated notes/graph/live cards against human rubrics and competitor outputs where lawful and practical.
- Record benchmark runs as non-secret artifacts; no private meeting content in Seeds.

Acceptance:
- A documented benchmark plan exists with datasets/fixtures, metrics, scoring, and run cadence.
- The benchmark can gate later roadmap work and expose regressions before release.
- Results identify which competitor capability each AudioGraph feature is trying to beat.

title: Calendar and prior-context pre-briefs from the temporal graph
description:
Build Granola-class pre-meeting briefs, but backed by AudioGraph's temporal graph and local/private configuration.

Scope:
- Calendar connector architecture for local calendar and optional cloud calendars.
- Match attendees, companies, recurring meetings, prior sessions, unresolved decisions, commitments, and open questions from the graph.
- Generate a brief before the meeting without exposing secrets or private context to unapproved providers.
- UI affordance for reviewing/editing the brief before capture starts.

Acceptance:
- Users can open an upcoming meeting and see a concise brief: who is attending, what happened last time, what is unresolved, and suggested questions.
- Brief generation uses saved provider credentials and honors local-only/BYOK modes.
- Missing calendar access degrades to manual meeting context without breaking capture.

- Per-session modes such as sales, research, recruiting, support, standup, and general notes.

- UI that is visible and controllable to the user, with clear audio/capture status.

Acceptance:
- In a live session, AudioGraph emits useful assist cards without waiting for the full meeting to end.
- Cards cite transcript spans or graph context when possible.
- Users can pause, hide, pin, dismiss, and ask follow-up questions without corrupting transcript/graph state.

title: Architecture session: cross-session meeting memory workspace and recall UX
description:

Scope:

- Search and Q&A over notes, transcript spans, speaker timeline, and graph revisions.
- Confidence/provenance model so users can inspect why a memory exists and what updated it.
- Retcon behavior when new transcripts revise older notes or relationships.

Acceptance:
- Architecture doc describes persisted objects, indexes, provenance, privacy boundary, and UX navigation model.
- Design avoids append-only duplicate memories; graph changes are revisioned/diffed.
- Follow-up implementation Seeds are split by storage, indexing, backend query API, and frontend workspace views.

competitive_memory_workspace_research_20.summary: Granola, Otter, MeetGeek, and Notta all make cross-meeting memory/search a post-session workspace, but most do it as document/search lists rather than a provenance-first temporal graph. acceptance_additions: After Meeting workspace has a memory/search view separate from the live capture shell.
Every memory object exposes transcript span, note, graph revision, confidence, and update history.
Cross-meeting Q&A cites meetings and spans, not just generated summaries.
Graph visualizations explain and filter memory; they are not the only navigation model.

title: Privacy-first sharing, redaction, ACLs, and export links
description:
Make sharing a strength instead of a liability. AudioGraph should beat meeting-note tools by making privacy state explicit and reversible.

Scope:

- Explicit ACL/sharing model for note links, exports, and team workspaces.
- Share previews that show exactly what recipients can see.
- Expiring links, revoke, copy-safe exports, and audit trail.

Acceptance:
- Users cannot accidentally share transcript quotes, graph facts, or hidden speaker data through note links.
- Shared artifacts preserve provenance where allowed and omit private data where redacted.
- Tests cover redaction, revocation, export, and link-permission edge cases.

priority_refinement_2026_06_25.summary: User clarified sharing/privacy product work can be later. Keep trust boundaries in architecture, but detailed sharing/redaction/ACL feature work is no longer a P2 competitive cutline.

competitive_privacy_default_research_202.summary: Competitor privacy research reinforces the original direction: AudioGraph should compete on explicit, reversible privacy defaults. Public/unlisted note links and opt-out training defaults are a known trust risk in AI notetaker products. Even if sharing/redaction remains later than core usability, the UX model should preserve local-first defaults and make data routes/sharing previews non-secret and inspectable.
acceptance_additions: Default share state remains private/off until explicit user action.
Share/export preview must show exactly which transcript spans, notes, graph facts, speakers, and metadata leave the device.
Training/model-use status is visible per provider/workspace where applicable.
Existing local-first single-user mode stays viable without cloud sharing.

title: Action item lifecycle and integration sync

Acceptance:

- Synced external tasks retain source provenance and do not leak redacted data.
- Integrations are provider/credential-gated and do not require hardcoded platform assumptions.

priority_refinement_2026_06_25.summary: User clarified integrations can be later. Keep action extraction in mind for live agent/post-meeting workflows, but external sync integrations should not compete with live memory/agent architecture for the next roadmap cutline.

competitive_action_review_research_2026_.summary: Fathom/Otter/Fireflies/MeetGeek consistently sell the post-call handoff: summaries, decisions, action items, follow-up emails, CRM/project updates. acceptance_additions: After Meeting view has a first-class actions/decisions review queue.
Suggested actions are editable/accept/reject with transcript-span provenance before external sync.
External integrations stay provider/credential-gated and can remain later than local action lifecycle.

title: Evaluate SurrealDB file-backed engines on Blacksmith before storage selectability
description:
Follow-up from audio-graph-48bb. The kv-mem adapter proves the repository shape, but file-backed SurrealKV and RocksDB engines need durability, binary-size, native-dependency, and packaging evidence on Linux, macOS, and Windows before any selectable/default storage switch. Acceptance: compare kv-surrealkv and kv-rocksdb features, build/link time, binary size, native dependencies, corruption/backup behavior, and Tauri packaging behavior on Blacksmith runners; document recommendation and keep FileMemoryRepository default unless all platform evidence is green.

--- EVIDENCE UPDATE 2026-06-27 (backlog-zero wave) ---
LOCAL CROSS-PLATFORM PROBE (docs/reviews/2b2c-local-linux-evidence-2026-06-27.md). Throwaway isolated builds, NOT wired into product:

title: Define bounded event-writer queues and repository backpressure policy
description: Follow-up from audio-graph-f2b6 review. TranscriptEventWriter and ProjectionEventWriter now support repository-backed sinks behind the same writer-thread/shutdown contract as the file path, but both file and repository paths still use std::sync::mpsc::channel, which is unbounded. If live DB-backed storage becomes selectable, a slow repository adapter could grow memory rather than applying explicit backpressure, dropping, or surfacing a degraded state. Scope: define queue limits, try_send or sync_channel behavior, metrics, UI diagnostics, and provider/session shutdown semantics for transcript/projection event writers. Acceptance: chosen queue policy is documented; tests cover slow sink behavior, full queue behavior, shutdown drain/drop semantics, and no secret/log leakage; FileMemoryRepository disk-full diagnostics remain file-specific; repository adapter failures surface as non-secret storage degraded diagnostics.

bounded_writer_queue_wave_2026_06_26.summary: Implemented a bounded non-blocking event-writer queue policy for TranscriptEventWriter and ProjectionEventWriter. Both file-backed and repository-backed event writers now use sync_channel with EVENT_WRITER_QUEUE_CAPACITY=2048, append via try_send, drop new events on full queues, track dropped counts, and emit a redacted persistence-queue-backpressure event on pressure transitions. Shutdown now sets the atomic flag and best-effort enqueues a sentinel with try_send so it cannot block behind a full queue. Projection runtime now enqueues the projection patch before saving materialized notes/graph, so queue-full rejection does not save materialized state without a replayable event. Modes should include local_only, byok_cloud, cloud_disabled_readiness_only, and org_promotion. Acceptance: ASR, LLM/projection, TTS, native S2S, live-assist, embeddings/future memory, and org sync routes refuse session-content transfers when blocked; no-content saved-key readiness/model catalog probes can remain allowed; tests cover representative provider clients and verify blocked calls emit redacted policy events instead of sending audio/text/graph context.

runtime_policy_wave_started_2026_06_26.summary: Starting a bounded Template A implementation wave for backend-enforced local-only/cloud-disabled runtime policy. Scope for this wave: discover current settings/provider/session seams, add the smallest Rust-owned policy contract that can block representative session-content provider routes while preserving no-content readiness/model checks, and record any broader ASR/TTS/S2S/embedding/org-sync gaps as Seeds rather than pretending one slice closes the whole policy surface.
constraints: Do not touch CI/release workflows from the dirty checkout.
Do not read or log plaintext credentials beyond existing backend-owned credential paths.
Preserve saved-key readiness/model discovery when no session content is transferred.
Keep React as display/control; enforcement belongs in Rust.

runtime_policy_entrypoint_wave_2026_06_2.summary: Added a Rust-owned privacy_mode setting with modes local_only, byok_cloud, cloud_disabled_readiness_only, and org_promotion. Current session-content entry points now enforce policy before cloud provider content transfer: start_transcribe gates ASR audio and LLM projection/extraction, chat and notes gate transcript/graph/prompt transfer, streaming chat gates cloud TTS speak-aloud, and Gemini notes/native converse gate audio/model-response transfer before consumer registration/connect. LLM executor jobs now carry allow_cloud_fallbacks so restricted modes cannot silently fall back from local providers to OpenRouter/API cloud clients. Readiness/model discovery paths were left ungated for no-content saved-key checks. Frontend Settings and ExpressSetup preserve privacy_mode without exposing secrets or adding a visible control in this slice.

title: Multiple tauri::test mock apps per process panic on gtk main-context (blocks command-layer tests in CI)
description:
FIXED on branch fix/gtk-test-harness-65f0 (2026-06-27), independently verified green. ROOT CAUSE: tao acquires the gtk main context on first tauri::Builder::build() and never releases it; the Rust harness runs each #[test] on its own thread even at --test-threads=1, so the 2nd command_test_app/mock_context app construction in a process panicked, poisoning process-global test locks and cascading 47 failures.

THREE-PART FIX: (1) poison-recovery — 49 process-global test-lock .lock().unwrap() sites converted to .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) [TEST_HOME_LOCK x35 in commands/state/sessions/speech/user_data, USAGE_TEST_LOCK x12 in sessions/usage, STORAGE_FLAG_LOCK x2 in persistence/io]; this alone stops any panic from cascading. (2) ONE gtk app per process — new pub(crate) fn shared_test_app_handle() in speech/mod.rs builds the tao app exactly once via OnceLock and leaks it 'static; the 3 speech app-tests (tests_status moonshine + 2 tests_integration) reuse the shared handle. (3) impl-extraction — start_capture/stop_capture/load_session split into thin #[tauri::command] wrappers calling *_impl(&AppState, &AppHandle); the 5 commands::tests now use an owned AppState::new() + the shared handle instead of a per-test app; command_test_app helper deleted.

VERIFICATION (independently re-run): cargo test --no-default-features --features cloud --lib -- --test-threads=1 => 1072 passed; 0 failed (was 1025/47). Clippy: 37 warnings (baseline preserved, 0 new). Each previously-failing test passes both in isolation and in-suite.

ENVIRONMENTAL NOTE: under WSL/xvfb the process exit code is 1 even with 0 failed — but this reproduces for a zero-gtk pure-logic test in isolation too, so it is a pre-existing WSL/xvfb harness artifact, not a test failure or a regression from this fix. Should be confirmed on Blacksmith Linux runners as part of the CI-evidence track.

UNBLOCKS: audio-graph-1d59 (the capture lifecycle tests now pass in-suite) and removes the test-evidence blocker for afca. NOT yet committed — the fix lives in the dirty working tree on its branch and folds into the commit-sequencing plan (docs/reviews/dirty-tree-commit-plan-2026-06-27.md) Phase G (commands.rs/speech).
closeReason: Fixed + verified, committed 0ded1c8 (poison-recovery on 49 test-lock sites + shared_test_app_handle OnceLock + start/stop/load_session *_impl(&AppState,&AppHandle) extraction; command_test_app deleted). cargo test --no-default-features --features cloud --lib --test-threads=1 = 1072 passed / 0 failed (was 47 failed). macOS ignores preserved. WSL exit-1-at-teardown confirmed environmental (zero-gtk test also exits 1 alone).

title: SettingsPage rewrite renders duplicate credential inputs — 23 SettingsPage.test.tsx failures (ambiguous findByLabelText)
description:
FOUND-BY: backlog-zero frontend commit verification (2026-06-27), branch fix/gtk-test-harness-65f0.

SYMPTOM: 23 of 642 frontend tests fail, ALL in src/components/SettingsPage.test.tsx. Backend is green (1072/0 Rust), tsc is clean (0 errors). Failure mode is uniform: TestingLibraryElementError: 'Found multiple elements with the text of: /access key id/i' (also /openrouter api key/i, /service account path/i, /deepgram api key/i). The test helper openCredentialInput() does within(scope).findByLabelText(label) and gets >1 match.

ROOT CAUSE: the in-flight SettingsPage.tsx rewrite (uncommitted dirty-tree work, M vs HEAD 5516202) renders the same labeled credential input in TWO places at once — the provider capability card AND the main provider section — so the accessible label is ambiguous within a scope. Matches the audit's flagged pattern (seed-audit-2026-06-27.md item 6: 'SettingsPage and ExpressSetup duplicate source-blocker/readiness/credential logic; every fix lands twice'). Likely the new SecretCredentialControl/ProviderReadinessPanel/capability-card components mount the credential control redundantly.

SCOPE: src/components/SettingsPage.tsx + SettingsPage.test.tsx (both M, uncommitted), plus the new untracked SecretCredentialControl.tsx / ProviderReadinessPanel.tsx / ModelCatalogPicker.tsx / AdvancedSettingsDisclosure.tsx the rewrite introduced. NOT caused by the gtk-fix work (that was backend-only; zero frontend files committed). Pre-existing in the dirty tree.

IMPACT: BLOCKS committing the frontend layer green (Phase H of dirty-tree-commit-plan-2026-06-27.md). The backend + foundation + docs already committed clean on the branch; the frontend cannot land green until this is resolved.

FIX DIRECTION (for the SettingsPage-rewrite owner — do NOT hack inline): either (a) render each credential control exactly once per provider (dedupe capability-card vs section), or (b) scope the inputs so labels are unique within their container (distinct aria-labels or scoped within() regions), and update openCredentialInput()/the tests to match. Decide whether capability cards own the credential control or the section does — the audit says pick one shared abstraction.

ACCEPTANCE: bun run test => 642/642 pass (0 SettingsPage failures); tsc clean; no duplicate accessible labels for any credential field within a provider scope; the capability-card<->section navigation tests (preserves AWS/OpenRouter/Gemini/Deepgram fields) pass.
closeReason: Fixed (test-only), committed eedd0d9. Root cause was query-side, not duplicate inputs: new SecretCredentialControl action buttons carry descriptive aria-labels embedding the field name (a11y feature), so findByLabelText matched input+buttons. Scoped queries with {selector:'input'} + readinessStatus() helper; production code byte-identical, a11y invariant (no two inputs share a label) holds. bun run test = 642/642, tsc 0.

title: Resolve VB-CABLE licensing for automated CI use (Windows live-audio smoke)

VB-Audio VB-CABLE is the only proven silent-unattended virtual audio device for stock Windows CI runners (WASAPI loopback alone fails: GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender)=ERROR_NOT_FOUND with no hardware). title: Add @sentry/browser webview capture gated by the same analytics toggle (ADR-0023 deferred v1 item)

triage_2026_08_14.phase: post-MVP observability; blocked by trustworthy Session Memory MVP completion
triage_2026_08_14.agent_brief:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Add privacy-gated browser/webview error capture through @sentry/browser after the core Session Memory MVP is complete.

**Current behavior:**
AudioGraph's opt-in analytics channel initializes the raw Rust Sentry SDK for backend diagnostics. Webview JavaScript errors are not captured, and @sentry/browser is not installed or initialized. The accepted analytics decision intentionally deferred browser capture while preserving one user-controlled analytics consent setting.

**Desired behavior:**
When and only when the existing analytics setting is enabled, initialize @sentry/browser in the webview using the same public DSN and privacy boundary as the backend. Runtime enable and disable transitions must affect both sides consistently. Browser events must be aggressively scrubbed so transcripts, notes, graph content, prompts, credentials, identifiers, usernames, URLs with sensitive data, request bodies, breadcrumbs, and arbitrary user text cannot leave the device.

**Key interfaces:**
- Existing analytics-enabled setting and runtime toggle — the single consent authority for backend and webview capture.
- Frontend analytics lifecycle — initialize once after consent, close or disable promptly when consent is withdrawn, and remain inert by default.
- Browser-event scrubber — enforce the same content-free diagnostics boundary as the backend rather than relying on SDK defaults.
- Application bootstrap and teardown — must not emit an event before settings hydration proves consent.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] @sentry/browser is absent from runtime behavior while analytics is off, including startup before settings hydration.
- [ ] Enabling analytics initializes browser capture once; disabling it prevents subsequent browser delivery without requiring restart.
- [ ] Browser and backend analytics follow the same persisted consent across restart.
- [ ] sendDefaultPii is false and request, user, breadcrumb, free-text, credential, transcript, note, graph, and prompt content is removed or replaced by bounded content-free classifications.
- [ ] Tests plant representative secrets and Session content in every retained browser-event field and prove none survives the scrubber.
- [ ] A controlled browser exception is delivered only after opt-in, while the equivalent pre-opt-in and post-disable exceptions are not delivered.
- [ ] The integration uses @sentry/browser directly and does not adopt tauri-plugin-sentry or change the backend SDK decision.
- [ ] Existing frontend gates and production packaging checks pass.

**Out of scope:**
- Native minidumps.
- Source-map or debug-symbol upload.
- Session replay, performance tracing, user analytics, or product telemetry.
- Changing the backend Sentry SDK architecture.
- Landing before the trustworthy Session Memory MVP acceptance boundary.

title: Tighten flaky clear_drops_in_flight_audio_frames test (test-only race)
description: Root-caused as a TEST-ONLY race (production Clear-suppression is correct via a round-trip happens-before: clearing.store(true) before the socket write, server sends trailing only after receiving Clear). Fix: require all 3 pre-clear frames (assert ==3 or loop on events.next() until 3 AudioChunks), drop the 500ms early-exit loophole. ~1/25-50 flake under multi_thread, 0/40 under --test-threads=1. No production change.

recommendations: Create two primary product modes: During Meeting and After Meeting; During Meeting should prioritize capture state, running notes, live transcript, and live assist; After Meeting should prioritize summary, actions, searchable transcript, graph diff/provenance, and exports.
Demote KnowledgeGraphViewer from default hero to an Analysis/Graph tab or secondary pane; the graph becomes proof/explanation, not the first useful artifact.
Replace three always-visible columns with a task-ranked shell: left compact capture/source strip, center notes/transcript/live-assist workspace, right contextual details only when selected.
Move token usage, projection runtime, data route, and backpressure into a Health/Diagnostics drawer/status menu except when blocking user action.
Add a one-click session path: choose mode + source + start; sample preview should demonstrate the final note/action/memory outcome before exposing provider details.
Validate at 1280px, 1024px, and narrow side-window sizes with screenshots and keyboard passes; acceptance should include no primary action hidden behind resizers or bottom diagnostics.

product_correction_universal_evidence_an.scope_expansion: Provenance is not limited to approved live-assist cards or transcript span ids. Temporal knowledge must support typed Evidence Annotations to every Session Artifact including Original Session Audio transcript revisions notes projection patches and graph state.
product_correction_universal_evidence_an.grounding_rule: Derived artifacts help navigate but a claim must retain a trace to canonical evidence; unavailable or deleted evidence remains explicit rather than silently severing the annotation.

unavailable_evidence_annotation_semantic.requirement: Evidence Annotation resolution returns Present or Unavailable Evidence with an exact reason; it never silently drops an annotation or treats deleted audio as retrievable.
unavailable_evidence_annotation_semantic.distinction: Unavailable Evidence is not a Knowledge Gap because grounding once existed even though the supporting artifact is no longer retained.

grounded_inference_provenance_expansion_.requirement: Promotion provenance must distinguish directly asserted knowledge from Grounded Inference and serialize the inference premises, Evidence Annotations, uncertainty, alternatives, counterevidence, temporal scope, and independent-review result.
grounded_inference_provenance_expansion_.anti_laundering_rule: An inferred premise must retain its transitive Inference Chain; repeated promotion or graph traversal must never collapse it into an asserted fact.
grounded_inference_provenance_expansion_.agent_contract: Recall and live-assist answers may use Grounded Inference but must label it as inference and expose its supporting evidence.
grounded_inference_provenance_expansion_.current_gap: Existing provenance and confidence fields do not encode origin or a reviewable premise chain.

title: Projection fallback chain misreports failure as 'mistral.rs LLM is not loaded' — last_error swallows the real OpenRouter error
description:
MANUAL-TEST FINDING (2026-07-06, Windows build 04e59bf, 4.5-min Deepgram capture).

SYMPTOM: 80 of 86 'Projection job generation failed' warnings say 'mistral.rs LLM is not loaded' — but the user's provider is OpenRouter and mistral.rs was never selected or loaded.

MECHANISM (src-tauri/src/llm/executor.rs run_projection_attempts ~:701): the chain for LlmProvider::OpenRouter is [openrouter, api, native, mistralrs]. On failure it returns only the LAST error. So when the OpenRouter attempt fails (the real cause — parse/decode errors), api + native + mistralrs also fail with their 'not configured/loaded' boilerplate, and the surfaced error is ALWAYS 'mistral.rs LLM is not loaded'. The real failure never reaches the log/UI. Diagnosability bug: made a real OpenRouter incident look like a local-model config problem.

FIX DIRECTION: keep the first error from the SELECTED provider (or join all attempt errors: 'openrouter: <err>; api: not configured; ...'). The selected provider's error is the one to surface; downstream 'not loaded' noise belongs at debug level.

RELATED same-session data: 103 successful backend outputs all provider=openrouter; 74 Graph + 12 Notes jobs failed. Companion seeds: parse-robustness (see 401-recovery + structured-output seeds this session).
closeReason: Shipped in PR #96 (squash a804570): run_projection_attempts returns the FIRST (selected-provider) error — kills the 'mistral.rs LLM is not loaded' masking that hid the real OpenRouter failure from the user's logs; downstream fallback errors demoted to debug; empty-chain text corrected. Gate round 2 fixed the same masking class in the new escalation fallback (producing backend's repair error surfaces raw, regression test added).

title: OpenRouter projection/extraction JSON frequently invalid: no structured-output enforcement + repair uses same failing backend
description:
MANUAL-TEST FINDING (2026-07-06, Windows, 4.5-min capture, model=openai/gpt-oss-120b via OpenRouter).

DATA: 103 projection backend outputs (all openrouter) but 86 generation failures + 6 'patch draft invalid and repair failed' (missing field id/tags/title) + 17 extraction failures (9 'error decoding response body', 8 missing field relations/target/name, invalid-null). Notes projections: 0 applied in the whole session — the During view showed no notes. Graph got 54 deltas through despite the noise.

MECHANISMS:
1. projection_openrouter (executor.rs ~:830) requests JSON with chat_completion_with_usage_cached(..., true, ...) — JSON *mode*, not a JSON *schema*. gpt-oss-120b emits schema-invalid patches (missing id/tags/title). Contrast ProjectionStructuredOutputMode::MistralRsJsonSchema which enforces. OpenRouter supports structured outputs (response_format json_schema + strict) on many models incl. gpt-oss.
2. Repair retries the SAME attempt backend with a repair prompt (run_projection_patch_with_attempts) — when the model is the problem, repair usually fails the same way (observed: 6/6 double-failures).
3. 'error decoding response body' (9x) = reqwest-level decode on /chat/completions — likely mid-body connection drop or non-JSON payload; there is no HTTP retry on the blocking extraction path (provider-connections review M4, PR #86 scope was WS only).

FIX DIRECTION: (a) send response_format=json_schema with the projection patch schema + strict on OpenRouter (fallback to json mode for models without support); (b) extraction M4 retry: bounded 2-3 attempt jittered retry on decode/timeout/429/5xx for the blocking extraction call; (c) repair escalates to next backend in chain instead of same-model retry; (d) consider defaulting projection model away from gpt-oss-120b or documenting model requirements.

EVIDENCE: audio-graph.log 12:54-12:59 session 63f86915; Sentry AUDIO-GRAPH-3 llm.openrouter.* events 192+.
closeReason: Shipped in PR #96 (squash a804570): OpenRouter structured outputs (response_format json_schema strict, schema >= validator via projection_patch_strict_json_schema, kind-partitioned); schema-rejection fallback with per-model session cache gated on model-level evidence only (404 under require_parameters); provider.require_parameters pinned for schema requests (Codex P2); repair escalates to next backend; body-decode folded into bounded retry. Cache-hint orthogonality test-asserted (ADR-0025 survives). 112 scoped tests. Restores notes generation (user session: 0 notes, 86 failures on gpt-oss-120b). Outer gate: 2 fix rounds. Follow-ups: a271, f01d.

title: Sentry AUDIO-GRAPH-3 groups unrelated events (info llm.openrouter.routed + frontend.invoke.error) into one issue — fingerprinting too coarse
description: OBSERVATION (2026-07-06): issue AUDIO-GRAPH-3 accumulated 197 events spanning at least: level=error frontend.invoke.error (provider=start_transcribe, the 401 loop) AND level=info llm.openrouter.routed (routing telemetry). These are unrelated surfaces sharing one Sentry issue, which (a) buries real errors under info-level routing beacons, (b) makes issue counts meaningless, (c) triggered 'new issue' noise. Likely cause: the native sentry client groups by message template/transaction rather than a per-event-name fingerprint, and ADR-0023 telemetry events are sent as 'default' type events at info level into the error stream. FIX DIRECTION: set explicit fingerprint = [event.name] (category+kind) for captureFrontendError/relay events; route info-level telemetry (routed/accounting beacons) to a separate logger or drop to breadcrumbs attached to real errors; keep level=error only for actionable failures. Verify grouping with two distinct event.names after the change.

ADR-0023 hardened in the P1 round: breadcrumb message+category now scrubbed through sanitize_tag_value (credential-shaped values dropped) with a premise-proving regression test. title: Notes patches discarded as stale during continuous speech — only land after a pause (DiscardedStaleAndStartedRepair churn)
description: MANUAL-TEST ROUND 3 (2026-07-07 23:06-23:10 session, build d5eaa91): the a324 schema fix WORKS for notes (structured_output_mode=OpenRouterJsonSchema on all 40 backend outputs; ZERO notes-kind generation failures vs 12 in round 2) — but of 23 completed Notes jobs, 22 were DiscardedStaleAndStartedRepair (staleness=MissingCurrentSpan) and only 1 reached CompletedCurrent, at 23:10:08 — 8s AFTER capture stopped. During ~3 min of continuous speech, every completed notes patch was stale-by-arrival because new transcript spans landed faster than generation completed; the During view shows nothing until the speaker pauses. Generation is no longer the bottleneck — the apply policy is. FIX DIRECTIONS (design decision): (a) apply stale notes patches progressively (mark them partial, let the repair overwrite) instead of discarding; (b) pin the basis window at job start and accept the patch for that window; (c) throttle span-revision-triggered discards (only discard if the patch's spans were REVISED, not merely appended-after). Evidence: log lines 2135+ pattern, session a26e85c0.

Classifier labels every hash difference AppendOnlyStale, including the same spans and revisions with a forged or corrupt basis hash. Hash the current-ledger subset covered by the basis first; mismatch is Revised TranscriptHashMismatch before checking appended spans.

title: Graph projection on gpt-oss-120b: ~50% response-decode failures + missing 'type' field escapes strict schema
description: MANUAL-TEST ROUND 3: all 20 projection generation failures were kind=Graph (notes clean): (1) 17 terminal 'error decoding response body' — the new bounded retry IS working (32 attempt-1 warns → 25 attempt-2 → ~11 rescued) but the failure is PERSISTENT not transient on graph calls (~50% rate), suggesting truncation: graph patches are much larger than notes — likely max_tokens ceiling or provider-side truncation of long schema-constrained output. Check the projection request's max_tokens for graph kind, and whether the decode error is reqwest body-truncation vs invalid JSON tail. (2) 6 'missing field type' failures (3 survived repair) DESPITE OpenRouterJsonSchema mode — either the graph kind's strict schema does not mark 'type' required at the right nesting level (audit projection_patch_strict_json_schema graph variant vs trusted_projection_patch_from_model_json's graph requirements), or the routed provider ignored the schema even with require_parameters (log the routed provider from the response metadata to distinguish). Graph still emitted 26 deltas — degraded, not dead. Session a26e85c0, build d5eaa91.

confirmed: OpenRouter defaults every request to 512 output tokens; Graph has no override.
ChoiceMessage.content is String although successful OpenRouter responses may contain null.
response.json and is_decode conflate malformed transport bodies with valid incompatible envelopes.
Schema-cached projection calls discard routing telemetry and success logs configured rather than served provider and model.
Graph strict schema already requires type for all variants.
safe_fix: Use a per-request Graph budget max configured 2048 for schema and JSON fallback only.
Read successful body as text and log only sanitized byte count request id shape category route finish reason and token counters.
Parse content as optional; null or empty is terminal missing_completion_content rather than a serde retry.
Retry only bounded transport body-read malformed or incomplete JSON conditions; valid incompatible envelopes are terminal.
Thread sanitized selected provider served model finish reason and reasoning token count through projection diagnostics without changing durable provenance.

title: Cargo.lock is gitignored — CI re-resolves deps every run; upstream releases can break all builds at any moment (aws-smithy-http incident)
description: INCIDENT (PR #97 run 28972645682): aws-smithy-http = "0.63" (range) floated to a new release that moved/removed the event_stream module → every Rust job on every OS failed identically, on a commit that touched only frontend files. Root cause: src-tauri/Cargo.lock is in .gitignore (line 11), so CI re-resolves the whole graph on every run and any upstream release can break or (worse) supply-chain-poison builds nondeterministically. Hotfix applied on PR #97: exact pin aws-smithy-http = "=0.63.6". REAL FIX (CI-policy change — surface to user for approval, never auto-merge): (a) commit src-tauri/Cargo.lock (Cargo team guidance for binaries/apps since 2023) + add --locked to all CI cargo invocations, or (b) minimum: --locked with a lockfile artifact. Also audit other open ranges (aws-sdk-* "1.102"/"1.101", aws-config "1.1") which have the same exposure. Relates: bfa8 (rsac drift), 2ef1 (time pin), 8eeb (PPA pin) — the repo has a pattern of unpinned-supply-chain seeds.

title: Crash consistency: make canonical event logs durable before live and materialized state advances
description: MVP data-integrity blocker found by the 2026-07-09 storage audit; child of audio-graph-5c57 and audio-graph-9c89. Default transcript/projection writers use buffered writeln and primarily flush at shutdown, while accepted enqueue can let the live ledger/materialized state advance; projection snapshots are atomically written and fsynced before the canonical projection event log is guaranteed durable. A process or power loss can therefore lose acknowledged transcript/projection events or leave notes/graph snapshots ahead of their replay source. Acceptance: define and document the durability boundary; canonical event append is framed and made crash-durable before corresponding live/materialized commit is acknowledged; snapshots never become authoritative ahead of their basis log; recovery detects/truncates partial tails and repairs or rejects ahead-of-log snapshots; batching may amortize fsync only with explicit bounded-loss semantics surfaced to UI; fault-injection tests cover kill/power-loss points, ENOSPC, short write, flush/fsync failure, restart replay, and no secret/content leakage in diagnostics.

title: Implement the direct noninteractive Windows Credential Manager v2 boundary
description: Replace the v2 keyring facade on Windows with an AudioGraph-owned boundary over CredReadW, CredWriteW, and CredDeleteW only. Explicit recovery performs only a noninteractive diagnosis because Windows has no generic credential-store unlock.

title: Represent degraded STT fidelity in Speech Span Revisions
description:
Make the provider-neutral Speech Span Revision contract honest for STT providers with fewer capabilities than Deepgram.

Acceptance:
- Final-text-only providers can emit app-owned stable span ids, monotonic revision/order, and source provenance without fabricating provider features.
- Timing records origin and precision (provider exact/coarse, app estimated, or unavailable).
- Confidence can be unavailable and records its origin when present.
- Turn boundaries and speaker/channel attribution record provider/app-derived/unavailable origin.
- Deepgram-like partial/final/turn-aware fixtures retain full fidelity.
- A final-only fixture proves notes/graph scheduling consumes the same normalized contract with explicit degraded capability state.
- Existing transcript replay and Projection Basis semantics remain deterministic and migration/versioning is explicit.
- Provider readiness describes the user-visible capability degradation; no provider becomes selectable from this schema change alone.

Scope is normalized schema, adapters, fixtures, migration, and readiness semantics. Do not add one-off downstream provider branches.

title: Wayfind trustworthy Deepgram-to-Finalized Session Memory
description:
## Destination

Produce an approved, implementation-ready specification for AudioGraph's first trustworthy provider-neutral path from one-action recording start through Deepgram Speech Span Revisions, Cerebras-class LLM projections, retained evidence, final refinement, and Finalized Session Memory in Review.

## Notes

Domain: Session Memory. Consult CONTEXT.md and accepted ADRs 0020 and 0027 through 0034 before resolving tickets. Treat the maintainer-approved Deepgram plus Cerebras vertical-slice constraints already recorded under the MVP hardening queue as inputs. The default LLM route may use Chat Completions, Messages, or Responses-style APIs; Cerebras direct and Cerebras through OpenRouter are the initial proof routes. Use domain-modeling and grilling for human decisions, prototype for state or UX models, and research for external provider facts. This map plans decisions only; implementation remains a later SDLC handoff.

Seeds tracker convention: each ticket carries an extensions.wayfinder_parent pointer to this map and blocks this map. Native Seeds dependencies define ticket-to-ticket ordering and the frontier.

## Decisions so far

## Not yet specified

- Operational concurrency, quota, and cost controls that only become sharp after projection scheduling and route capabilities are decided.
- Legacy Session migration and repair policy after the canonical artifact and finalization contracts are complete.
- Exact export and recovery UX after Finalized, Finalization Blocked, Evidence Annotation, and Unavailable Evidence behavior is specified.

## Out of scope

- World Promotion and reconciliation into the User World; this receives its own map after trustworthy Finalized Session Memory exists.
- Realtime speech-to-speech assistance and proactive in-call coaching.
- Broad provider enablement beyond the provider-neutral contracts and the initial Deepgram plus Cerebras/OpenRouter proof routes.
- Implementing the destination; this map ends at a decision-complete specification and executable handoff.
